## Importing data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

Setting up path

```{r}
getwd()
#setwd("enterpathhere")
```

Importing multiple csv files

1.  the variable "files" is a vector containing filenames from group3_data folder
2.  read_onefile is a function for reading one csv file
    - col_names assign the dataframe column names to be "key" and "value". The datafile have no header, without this, R will assign first row to be column name

    - show_col_types = FALSE mutes the notification after running the read_csv commands. This is useful as will be iteratring on multiple files

    - pivot wider

    - mutate(file = basename(f)) is adding a new column containing the filename

    - relocate move the file column to the frist column of our dataframe
3.  map_dfr(x, y) runs the function y to vector x and put each output as new rows

```{r}
files <- list.files("../group3_data/", pattern ="\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
#group3_data is analysis files not found in github

read_onefile <- function(f) {
  read_csv(f, col_names = c("key","value"),
           show_col_types = FALSE) %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from = key, values_from =value) %>% 
    mutate(file = basename(f)) %>% 
    relocate(file, .before = 1)
}

dat <- map_dfr(files, read_onefile)
data <- dat
```

Inspecting and correcting erronous column name\
- Note the typoed column gene_Acccesion_id, heart, kidney, and pvalue\
- We will first display rows with erronous error and impute them

```{r}
#gene_accession_id
data %>%
  filter(!is.na(gene_Accession_id)) %>% 
  select(gene_accession_id, gene_Accession_id) 

data <- data %>%
  mutate(gene_accession_id = coalesce(gene_accession_id, gene_Accession_id)) %>%
  select(-gene_Accession_id)

#lacz_heart
data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(heart)) %>% 
  select(lacz_heart, heart)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(lacz_heart = coalesce(lacz_heart, heart)) %>%
  select(-heart)

#lacz_kidney
data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(kidney)) %>% 
  select(lacz_kidney, kidney)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(lacz_kidney = coalesce(lacz_kidney, kidney)) %>%
  select(-kidney)

#p_value
data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(pvalue)) %>% 
  select(p_value, pvalue)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(p_value = coalesce(p_value, pvalue)) %>%
  select(-pvalue)
```

Imputing other txt files

1.  trim_ws removes spaces from the beginning and end of each value
2.  rename changes column name. Since both parameter and procedure have col name called names and description, we change them as not to confuse each other
3.  comment = "\#" ignore all comments from the file. In disease information there are brief comments
4.  col_names. Since the col_names have no header, we assign our own colnames

```{r}
parameter <- read_csv("../IMPC_parameter_description.txt", trim_ws = TRUE) %>%  
  rename(param_name = name, param_description = description)
procedure <- read_csv("../IMPC_procedure.txt", trim_ws = TRUE) %>%  
  rename(proc_name = name, proc_desc = description)
disease <- read_tsv("../Disease_information.txt",
                    comment = "#",
                    col_names = c("human_symbol","human_name","hgnc_id",
                                  "do_term","do_id","mouse_genotypes",
                                  "mouse_symbol","mgi_id"))
bespoke <- read_tsv("../bespokeTask_GO.txt",
                    skip = 1,
                    col_names = c("DB","DB_obj_id","DB_obj_symbol","Relation",
                    "GO_id","DB_reference","evidence_code","with_from",
                    "aspect","DB_obj_name", "DB_obj_synonym", "DB_obj_type",
                    "taxon","date","assigned_by","annotation_exp",
                    "Gene_product_formid"))

```

Checking the dimension of all our imported data.\
Notice all our data have different dimension, there will be many to many relationship

```{r}
dim(data)

dim(disease)
dim(bespoke)
```

Joining data

***this preliminary joining data serves only for trying to understand how these files relate to one another and will not be used in further analysis, it will not be included in the precleaned.Rdata as well***

1.  join main data to parameter by paramater id
2.  join main data to procedure by imcParameterOrigId
3.  join main data to disease by gene_accession_id

join_param : data + paramater + procedure\
join_disease : data + disease\
join_all : data + parameter + procedure + disease

Notice the warning that many rows are duplicated since they have multiple match in the other table. So I assume we should not join these tables, but its nice to help make sense of the data

```{r}
join_param <- data %>% 
  left_join(parameter, by = c("parameter_stable_id" = "parameterId")) %>% 
  left_join(procedure, by = "impcParameterOrigId")

#assign variable containing all column name from disease table
disease_cols <- setdiff(names(disease), "mgi_id")

join_disease <- data %>% 
  left_join(disease, by = c("gene_accession_id" = "mgi_id")) %>% 
  relocate(all_of(disease_cols), .after = 4)


join_all <- data %>% 
  left_join(parameter, by = c("parameter_stable_id" = "parameterId")) %>% 
  left_join(procedure, by = "impcParameterOrigId") %>% 
  left_join(disease, by = c("gene_accession_id" = "mgi_id")) %>% 
  relocate(all_of(disease_cols), .after = 4)
```

Export Data as R.data

```{r}
precleaned_data <- data
precleaned_parameter <- parameter
precleaned_procedure <- procedure
precleaned_disease <- disease
precleaned_bespoke <- bespoke

save(precleaned_data, precleaned_disease, precleaned_procedure,
     precleaned_parameter, precleaned_bespoke, file = "precleaned.RData")

```
